source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Rear Suspension and Drive Line, p.4-4

procedures.title: Corvette rear suspension: general description
notes: Each rear spindle is driven by a tubular drive shaft with a U-joint at both ends; the outer end bolts by flange to a splined spindle flange, the inner end bolts to the differential side gear yoke.
Each spindle support carries an inner and an outer tapered roller bearing; bearing adjustment is by a spacer plus a shim of chosen thickness between the bearings.

Forged fork-shaped brackets on the spindle supports take the outer ends of the rubber-bushed strut rods; the strut rods run sideways to a bracket bolted under the carrier, where an eccentric cam at the inner mount sets rear camber.
Shock absorbers (direct, double-acting) mount at the top eye to a frame bracket and at the bottom eye to a threaded stud on the strut rod mounting shaft.

The multi-leaf spring is clamp-bolted at its center to a mounting face under the carrier cover; each end of the main leaf has a hole for the link bolt to the rear of the torque control arm. The spring has full-length liners.
An optional stabilizer shaft attaches to the upper rear of the torque control arms and runs rearward to two rubber-bushed brackets on the frame.

procedures.title: Rear suspension: periodic inspection
steps: Check the condition of the suspension bushings.
Check that the suspension attaching bolts are tight.
Look over all components for defects.
notes: No scheduled maintenance or adjustment is needed for the rear suspension parts.
